verdict.tagline: Build a car from loose parts and survive rural Finnish life.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep mechanical assembly challenges
you like gritty open world survival sandboxes
you are willing to consult external guides
not_for_you_if: you expect an in-game tutorial or instructions
you need reliable controller support for cameras
you cannot stand frustrating physics bugs

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment shifts positively as time spent with the game increases.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Initial players struggle with the steep learning curve, awkward controls, and absence of tutorials.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks a tutorial or instructions for core systems and vehicle building.

citations.review_text: Watched a few stremers play and decided to buy. Not intuitive at all, had no clue how to advance, controls, how to build the car, nothing..... which I get is intended. But made it frustrating/boring for me and my son who wanted the game.

I think this game is probably enjoyable to a very specific type of player, but without a tutorial getting you acquainted with the game it's pretty unintelligible (which seems to be intentional).

Here was my experience:
- go to the city using the tractor (everything is interactive other than the gear shift so figure out you are forced to use keybinds for that somehow)
- arrive at night, everything is closed except the diner
- thirst maxed, dirtiness maxed, no way to fix either of those
  - no source of water you can drink from
  - coffee at the shop doesn't fix thirst
  - convenience store closed at can't ask the owner (who handles the cafe) to buy water
  - one beer heals about 10% of your thirst meter so only option is to be max thirst or piss drunk
- try to fill tractor with gas
- no interactions at the gas station work
- finally give up and lookup how you are meant to use the gas station and find out it is closed at night
- my only options at this point seemed to be to leave the game afk until morning, or close the game

The game's difficulty seems to come from withholding information, preventing experimentation, and punishing reasonable assumptions.

Maybe some day I'll follow a tutorial closely and get to the fun parts of the game, but as a player that prefers to avoid following wiki's and likes games that stand on their own two feet, I'm not really looking forward to that (the game also punishes external tool usage since there is no ability to pause from what I can tell)

incredibly boring and overhyped. game is trash. 
controls are terrible, hitboxes on items are way to small, zero tutorial so i dont know what im doing, and no clear direction.

the game is supposed to be "retro" but instead just feels poorly made.
refunded.

citations.review_text: Good game... needs some work on physics.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players master manual car building and repairs without built-in guides.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention needing to manually assemble the car from hundreds of loose parts without any built-in tutorials or guides.

citations.review_text:
My Summer Car is a really great and unique game that can keep you entertained for many hours. What I like most is that you don't get a finished car – you have to build it almost completely from scratch yourself. At first, this can be really complicated, especially if you don't have any previous knowledge of how engines are built. However, after a few attempts, you start getting the hang of it and understand better where everything is supposed to go.

A big advantage is that building the car can actually teach you the basics of how an engine is constructed and how its different components work together. The game doesn't hold your hand and requires you to figure out the mechanics yourself.

I also really like how breakdowns work. When the car breaks down, you can't just press a button and suddenly have everything working again. You have to find the problem yourself, remove the necessary parts, and replace whatever is damaged. Sometimes the problem is serious enough that you have to take apart a large part of the engine and then put everything back together correctly. This makes every repair feel rewarding, especially when the car finally starts after several attempts and you can drive it again.

The game isn't only about building and repairing cars, either. You also have to take care of your character by eating, drinking, sleeping, and keeping yourself clean. There are also several interesting jobs that allow you to earn money. You can chop firewood and deliver it to a specific location, or even pump out septic tanks. These activities make the game world feel more alive, while the money you earn can be spent on improving your car.

My Summer Car also has a story, but one of the best things about it is that you don't have to focus on it if you don't want to. At the beginning, we learn that the house we live in belongs to our parents, who have gone on vacation, while we receive a blue car from our uncle. After a few hours of playing, the car is fully in our possession. …

My Summer Car is the ultimate car owning, building, fixing, tuning, maintenance AND permadeath life survival simulator. You start the game with hundreds of loose parts and assemble both car and engine.

Game is fun and pretty cool but there is some issues that really have been aggrieving me for a while, the graphics of the game are very broken for my computer specifically with shadows just flickering out and having very noticeable artefacting and movement that causes a genuine seizure risk when looked at. And I've also had issues with the game's physics but that less so than the shadows. I've tried basically everything to fix the shadows but its a issue with the version of Unity that cant really be fixed. I know the game is made by like 1 guy but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. the issues with the shadows caused me a lot of trouble, since without sun shadows the interior lights don't exist which causes the game to look like vomit.

Besides the graphics issues I've had I also really wish there was some form of item carry system since hauling more than 2 items is beyond the amount of being a pain in the ass than it should be, and this issue really plagues you when you try and move stuff later. The game also just doesn't have a built in guide for building the car and without an external list of where the bolts, electrics, and how to tune the car you're going to be messing around and dying for a while.

Genuinely I gotta send billions of years of drought to the lands of every person I messaged when trying to get help with the graphics issues since telling me over and over that the game is indie doesn't help me try and fix the damn issues with the shadows.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players embrace diverse survival activities and mod support despite unpredictable physics.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering bugs and unpredictable physics while playing.

citations.review_text: Love this game, even if sometime I hate it due to the stupid physics (and AI, but I guess it's lore friendly from alcohol everywhere) . And the best part is, it's kinda remind my childhood, living away from everything and had to fix my junk car, beside that doing jobs like driving a tractor with a trailer loaded of firewood. Anyway, the game is fun, lot of customization available ingame and from the game files, modding the game is possible (there are some really needed mods for QoL improvements ). A must have !

If you like driving around, fixing your engine every 200 kilometers, brewing your own booze, driving your drunk friend home at 2:00AM or customizing your car to your own preferences, then this game is for you.

MSC is one of the most unique driving and survival games out there! Building your Satsuma screw by screw and then finally taking it on a test drive is incredibly rewarding.

It has its ups and downs, like annoying bugs but those bugs make the best memories. Just remember not to drive on the dirt roads during the weekend, or you will get hit by a rally driver while driving your grandma to church...

Its one of those games that will make you laught, spam Alt + F4 and question your life choices but then you´ll look at the clock and realize that you have been playing for 5 hours instead of 5 minutes. Dont forget to press the M and N keys to discover the beauty of the Finnish langauge.

10/10. Would reccommend. Perkele!

It took me a lot of patience to build and tune the Satsuma. I probably would have quit the game without ever finishing the car if it weren't for the variety of things you can do. You have to plan your days, buy food, cigarettes, alcohol, household supplies, and all the parts needed to assemble the car.
To afford all of this, the game offers plenty of ways to earn money. You can buy yeast and sugar to brew homemade "sugar wine" and sell it to a local guy for decent cash, pump out septic tanks, chop and sell firewood, drive home the drunk guy who calls you in the middle of the night, and much more.
Despite its simple appearance, the game is actually a very detailed life simulator of a young village car enthusiast

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks any tutorial or instructions, placing players into the experience without guidance.

citations.review_text:
It took me over 20 hours just to build the Satsuma, and somehow I still managed to make the entire process enjoyable. The game doesn't hold your hand, so you actually have to figure out where everything goes, what needs to be adjusted, and why the car refuses to start after you've spent hours putting it together. One tiny mistake can mean taking half the car apart just to figure out what you did wrong. That's what makes My Summer Car so entertaining. It's frustrating, confusing, and sometimes absolutely ridiculous, but finally getting the Satsuma running after spending hours working on it feels incredibly rewarding. The game turns something as simple as building a car into an entire survival experience filled with mistakes, suffering, and the occasional feeling of accomplishment. I originally thought I was going to casually build a car and drive around Finland. Instead, I spent 20+ hours questioning every decision I've ever made. Despite that, I genuinely enjoyed it. My Summer Car is definitely not an easy game, but that's exactly what makes it memorable.

10/10 would play again :3

its a pretty good game ngl, but a nice little warning. the game has no tutorial, no instructions, nothing. they kinda just throw you in there and say "now go, play" but i figured it out after a bit. pretty fun, simple, and yeah.
